questions.question: The average height of 50 randomly chosen adults is 171 cm. This number is a...
questions.explanation: It is computed from a sample, so it is a statistic. A parameter would describe the entire population.

questions.question: Which symbol stands for the SAMPLE mean?
questions.explanation: x̄ (x-bar) is the sample mean. μ (mu) is the population mean. Remember: Greek letters go with parameters, Roman letters with statistics.

questions.question: Two researchers each take a random sample from the same population and get different sample means. What does this show?
options: One of them made a mistake
questions.explanation: Different random samples give different statistics. The population mean (the parameter) stays fixed. The gap is sampling error, which is expected.

questions.question: Which action tends to REDUCE sampling error?
questions.explanation: Larger random samples cluster closer to the parameter. Volunteers or a single location introduce bias, which more data cannot cure.

questions.question: A survey outside a gym is used to claim how often 'people in the city' exercise. What is the main problem?
options: Bias, because the sample is not representative
questions.explanation: Gym-goers exercise more than average, so the sample tilts one way. That systematic tilt is bias. A bigger sample from the same place would repeat the same mistake.

questions.question: For a sample, the standard deviation divides the sum of squared deviations by...
questions.explanation: Sample values sit closer to their own mean than to the true population mean, so dividing by n would understate the spread. Dividing by n − 1 (Bessel's correction) corrects that.
